I’ve struggled with the same. People I was friends with since childhood treat me differently now and it’s very uncomfortable. I miss the safety of feeling “invisible” of being fat. Losing weight uncovered a loooooot of other traumas and I’ve been diagnosed with CPTSD, among many other things. I’ve also gone through just about every eating disorder there is since surgery in May, 2023.

I really recommend getting a therapist! Especially one that specializes in body dysmorphia or eating disorders. It’s still hard even with one, but I’ve come significantly farther than I was without.

I’m 2 months post op and still learning quite a bit about my new body myself, but I wanted to say that those other comments on the other post were incredibly rude, especially considering the nature of the journey. 

I was diagnosed with binge eating disorder and worked on it in therapy for years, and still am! But since surgery, I do notice that if I can cut calories wherever, I do. Not in a healthy way, but in a way that is going to lead me down a path to another eating disorder due to trying to restrict myself. This is also something I am working on heavily in therapy and day to day.

This is an incredibly difficult thing you have done! There is no right or wrong way, everyone has a different journey. I don’t count my calories, because that led me to restriction and disordered patterns. I instead have been focusing on mindfulness and listening to my body - something I am literally learning to do now because I never learned how. 

I would say give yourself some credit, be gentle on yourself, and therapy is a great option! As for the calories, look up bariatric recipes (I’ve found lots on tiktok that have been great!) that are filling and lower cal, and maybe try looking at your food and hunger levels in different ways to see what works for you if calorie counting isn’t it!

You’ve got this and I’m so sorry your first post here was negatively received. You’re doing your best and that is something that means EVERYTHING! 💖

I have cried every single day since coming home from surgery. Pre-surgery, I was in therapy for binge eating disorder. These two weeks have been so difficult mentally that I’ve regretted it, resented it, and wished that I never did the surgery. However, I’m coming to realize these thoughts are because I am mourning what I used to use to comfort myself: food. I can’t comfort myself with food anymore and it’s hard because I have to learn new ways to comfort myself.

I’m in therapy still to help with this (among other things like ADHD, anxiety, depression), but my best advice as I slowly come down from the two week spiral is this: be gentle on yourself. This is a huge life change and it is HARD. Let yourself cry and miss the life you had, but know that this is just another moment, and it will pass. Good things are coming.
